newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany faces new strike threat in work-hours row.
newsitem.headline: Germany faces new strike threat in work-hours row.

text.p: Germany faced the risk of a new bout of industrial unrest on Wednesday as IG Metall, its largest trade union with 2.7 million members, said it was ready to back strikes in a new row over work-hours.

The metal and engineering sector union said in a statement it was ready to strike to push through proposals allowing workers to retire early. IG Metall already said at the weekend strikes to secure a general 32-hour week were possible.
"It is clear that working time cuts must be put in place by late-1998 to early 1999 as part of the fight against unemployment," the union's board said in a statement.
"If necessary, this proposal (on early retirement) can be implemented through strikes," IG Metall said in a statement.

IG Metall and other major trade unions made it clear at a high-profile employment conference in Berlin last week that they saw reduced working hours and overtime as the main ways to reach a previously-agreed goal between unions, employers and the government of halving joblessness by the year 2000.
Equally clear has been the opposition of Bonn and employer groups to such measures. They argue that they would only make German labour more expensive and increase the long-term risk of unemployment.
Germany has in recent months been hit by industrial unrest in the coal mining and steel sectors and saw widespread protests against cuts to sick pay entitlements introduced last October.
